cases.description: Both entry and exit trades are null. The default string representation should show the literal "null" for each part.
Only the entry trade is set (non‑null). The toString() should concatenate the entry's toString() value and the literal "null" for the exit.
Only the exit trade is set (non‑null). The method should display "null" for the entry and the exit's toString() value.
Both entry and exit trades are non‑null. The resulting string must contain the entry's toString() followed by a space, the word "exit:" and the exit's toString().

Entry trade's toString() returns an empty string while exit trade is a normal non‑null Trade. The method should concatenate the empty entry string with the literal "exit:" and the exit's toString() value.
The entry Trade object's toString() method is overridden to throw an IllegalStateException. When Position.toString() is invoked, the exception should be propagated unchanged.
The entry Trade object's toString() method is overridden to throw a NullPointerException. Position.toString() must not catch it; the same exception should be thrown to the caller.
The exit Trade object's toString() method is overridden to throw a generic RuntimeException. Position.toString() should propagate this exception.

group: Position.toString() - both entry and exit toString throw

cases.description: Both entry and exit Trade objects have toString() implementations that throw exceptions, but entry's exception (IllegalStateException) occurs first. Position.toString() should propagate the first encountered exception.
